status: machine-readable — only for the next AI session, not for human reading. Human-readable history/decisions live in PLAN.md and implementation-notes.md.
convention: This file carries POINTERS AND TRAPS, not retellings. A задача is cited by its section in PLAN.md or SPEC.md, never paraphrased here: a paraphrase is a second copy of the truth and it drifts (it already did once, for routing_lists). What belongs here instead: file and symbol pointers, measured facts, rejected shapes with their arguments, and the traps that cost the last passes time. Written down in full in implementation-notes.md, section 'doclint — утверждение документа о состоянии обязано опираться на исполнимое'.

measurement_vs_inference.rule: A measurement and the conclusion drawn from it are TWO statements, and this file must keep them apart. Record what was run and what it printed; record separately what you concluded, and name the steps between. A conclusion written as if it were the measurement is inherited by the next pass as measured fact.
measurement_vs_inference.why_this_block_exists: The previous HANDOFF said, citing a live run, that the agent holds the store's exclusive flock for its whole life and therefore `hop nodes` refuses while the tunnel is up. The run was real and still reproduces: `flock -x <root>/.lock sleep 8 &` then `hop nodes` → exit 1 after 5043 ms. The conclusion was wrong, and two inference steps did the damage: (1) 'the agent holds the store' → 'the agent holds the lock' — `store.Open` takes no lock, `load()` reads all three files without one, and the lock lives inside `transact`, per transaction (measured: 559 transactions, mean 1.05 ms); (2) 'the lock is held' → 'a reader waits' — a reader takes no lock at all. Both steps were invisible because the sentence read like a measurement.

closed_this_pass.premise_refuted: See measurement_vs_inference above. The task's stated blocker did not exist; the task survived it with a different, measured reason: the store holds a SLICE of liveness (§2) that reaches disk no more than once per 30 s (healthDebounce, healthPersistEvery), so a client reading the store next to a live agent sees stale state while the current state sits with the process it did not ask.
closed_this_pass.defect_found_and_fixed: The same run found a real one, and not the one being looked for: with the store busy, `hop nodes` printed all 201 lines of its answer and THEN returned 1 — reading needs no lock, but `Store.Close` took one unconditionally. `Close` now takes the lock only when there is something to write (internal/store/store.go). A refusal after the answer is already printed is a lie about one's own success, and §5.9's exit codes are what monitoring reads.
closed_this_pass.shape: Frames, not pages. Measured, reproducible with `go test ./cmd/hop -run TestW65Measure -v -count=1` (cmd/hop/measure_test.go): 200 nodes serialize to 64941 bytes against the 65536-byte §3.1 frame — 595 bytes of headroom, one percent, and accidental: names ten characters longer overflow it. A page needs a cursor into a list that changes between requests (§5.8), so page two arrives from a different composition and the picture never existed at any instant. Granularity is one frame per node: a batch has a size that will silently drift from the limit, a node does not (325 bytes against 65536). One assembly for both callers: store.GroupNodesView + Store.FullView in internal/store/view.go.
closed_this_pass.probe_stays_a_store_reader: Three arguments, the third decides: (1) probe is needed exactly where the agent's own refusal cannot say whose it is; (2) it is the only place exit code 3 is observable without an agent, and W56's guard rests on that; (3) with a live agent, a second probe on top of the §6.5 schedule is the full subscription sweep §6.5 exists to prevent — 4000 connections per hour against 870.
closed_this_pass.controller_correction: None. The controller re-measured the 200-node figure independently (60801 bytes with typical provider names, 63601 with longer ones, against the pass's 64941 including the group envelope) and reproduced the lock measurement; both hold. The controller's own negative control — truncating the stream after the fifth node, i.e. SILENT data loss rather than a refusal — reddens W65: 'узлов доехало 5 из 200'.

acceptance_review.measured: Final main: go test ./... green; the full internal/l3 package under `HOP_L3=1 unshare -Urn` run TWICE with a stray socket deliberately left at the shared path — 19 tests, zero skips, both runs green; doclint clean; go vet, gofmt -l and realtimelint identical to the baseline captured before the round. negcheck (48 policies) run at the end.
acceptance_review.stand_isolation: The second hole, and the one no single pass could have seen: `unshare -Urn` isolates the network and user namespaces but NOT $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR. internal/l3 started `hop agent` without -client-socket, so every L3 agent bound the machine-global ipc.DefaultClientPath and concurrent runs on one machine collided there. It stayed invisible because `hop status` silently falls back to the service socket when the client dial fails; W68's `hop up` step cannot fall back and is the first stand verb to expose it. Fixed in internal/l3/harness_test.go (per-test <tempdir>/c.sock threaded through commandAgent, startAgent, phaseAt), plus tunnel_test.go's tryAttach and autoconnect_test.go's three call sites. This is the same class as the earlier HOP_STORE finding: name what unshare does NOT isolate before trusting a stand.
acceptance_review.controller_rule_applied: Every incoming test whose subject is 'the mechanism exists' was reddened by hand: W65 (stream truncated after the fifth node — silent loss, not a refusal), W68 (wiring pulled from main.go), the grammar guard (stand calling a bogus verb, and a bogus flag). The 200-node figure and the lock measurement were re-run independently rather than accepted from the report.

parallel_passes_trap.what_the_zones_CANNOT_catch: Two classes, both seen live. parallel_passes_trap.rule_for_the_next_parallel_run: Hand out registry numbers in advance and require them in test names; name the zones per-file; require appends to the END of shared Go lists; expect to resolve document tails by hand; name in advance which passes consume an interface another may change; and re-run the L3 suite on the MERGED tree, twice, with a stray socket left at the shared path.

next_task.name: `store.Open` берёт замок ради подметания, когда писатель жив
next_task.why_first: Measured, reproduced, and it is the same class the nodes-socket pass already fixed in Close — only on the way in instead of on the way out. store.Open calls hasTempGarbage() (internal/store/store.go) BEFORE transact: atomic write creates a temp file in the store directory for the duration of write+rename, and a reader whose Open lands in that window mistakes the writer's live file for garbage from a killed process, takes the lock and goes sweeping. lock.acquire polls every 50 ms, which is where the granularity of the outlier comes from.
next_task.measured: With a writer running without pause: max lock hold 51 ms, `hop nodes` worst case 1.209 s. Same model under HOP_DISABLE=atomic_write (no temp files at all): 1.3 ms and 6 ms. The outlier disappears with the temp files, so the cause is not the scheduler. Reproduce with cmd/hop/measure_test.go.
next_task.shape_question: The conservative fix named by the pass that found it: try the sweep lock NON-blockingly and skip sweeping when it is busy — a busy lock means the writer is alive and the file is its own, not an orphan. Decide whether that is right, or whether the garbage check belongs after the lock entirely.
next_task.not_urgent_but_real: lockTimeout is 5 s and the observed worst case is 1.2 s under a model writing ~300× more often than the product (persistHealth writes once per 30 s). It is a latency defect today, not an outage. The pass that found it deliberately did not fix it: it had already touched internal/store once beyond its task and would not widen twice.

queue.task: `hop up` внутри окна orphaned отказывает состоянием, а не смыслом
queue.provenance: Reported by a parallel session running the binaries live under unshare -Urn; NOT reproduced by the controller. The mechanism was confirmed by reading, the reproduction was not run — keep those apart (see measurement_vs_inference).
queue.what: Kill the agent while the tunnel is up, without `hop down` (Detach, not Stop — the interface is meant to survive, T24). The next `hop up` fails with `tunnel: операция недопустима в текущем состоянии: orphaned, ожидалось down`.
queue.mechanism_read_not_measured: cmd/hop/transport.go `acquire` tries Attach by token first and falls back to `Start` (§6.2, T24). internal/tunnel/tunnel.go:215 lets Attach in only from Orphaned; Start refuses unless the phase is down. So the failure needs BOTH halves: the reattach lost its token (a fresh token file, e.g. what the L3 stand hands each agent) AND the tunnel is still inside its orphan deadline. Once orphan_deadline expires the tunnel is torn down and Start works again.
queue.why_it_is_a_defect_anyway: The user is shown a state-machine sentence about a phase they have no verb to observe or clear. §5.6 requires a refusal to say what it is: within the orphan window with the token gone, the honest answer names the deadline and offers the way out, and the way out has to exist. Decide whether `hop up` should wait out the deadline, whether a verb should drop an orphan deliberately, or whether the token should be recoverable — that decision is the task.

notes.doclint: Fast. CI runs it as `go run ./cmd/doclint -git=false .` — a checkout has neither the pass branches nor the full history, so the git half is off there and on locally.
notes.negcheck: runs every guard twice (with/without its policy) via `go test -count=1`; 48 policies as of this pass, ~25-35 min wall clock — expected, not a hang; don't rely on go test's cache. It needs permission to listen on loopback: a network-restricted sandbox creates false oracle defects. There is no per-policy selection: for a per-task gate run the new policy's own guard under HOP_DISABLE=<name> by hand; the controller runs the full one at the end.
notes.realtimelint: does not accept ./... as an argument — pass literally `.`
notes.l3_how_to_run: `go test -c -o /tmp/l3.test ./internal/l3` then `HOP_L3=1 unshare -Urn /tmp/l3.test` (add `-test.v -test.run '<pattern>'` to scope it). No root needed — unshare -Urn grants CAP_NET_ADMIN in a fresh netns. Reuse the built binary across runs. WITHOUT -test.v the package prints only a final PASS, and a fully-skipped package prints the same PASS: count `--- PASS` lines (19 as of this pass, zero SKIP) before believing it ran. Name what unshare does NOT isolate: $HOME (hence per-test HOP_STORE) and $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR (hence per-test -client-socket).
notes.known_red_that_is_not_yours: go vet ./... is red at internal/engine/dialer.go (copylocks in xray-core's SocketConfig). realtimelint is red with 3 hits in internal/dnstest/realserver_test.go. gofmt -l ./internal reports internal/l2/dns_test.go. All three predate these passes; the honest gate is 'no NEW findings', compared on the full output rather than the exit code. Capture the baseline before starting — it makes acceptance a diff instead of a judgement.
notes.flake: internal/l2 TestT10SlowNodeKeepsConnectionAlive flakes on timing under load. internal/health TestA22PinnedNodeIsNotReplacedWhenDead, measured on untouched a6221d3 so it belongs to no pass: clean without -race and clean under -race up to 5 repetitions, reddens from 10 (1 run in 3), always at health_test.go:623. Both are a fake clock against someone else's goroutine.
notes.what_is_not_a_flake: cmd/hop/measure_test.go compares against time in exactly one place — `hop nodes` must return 0 — and the margin there is three orders of magnitude. A refusal in that test is a regression, not load. The 'longest held' numbers it logs are not assertions and move freely on a busy machine.
